common_assumptions: File contents are current and unchanged between successive tool calls
Truncated tool output (head -N pattern) is sufficient for decision-making
TypeScript type-check passing implies feature-level correctness
First grep from a scoped directory is comprehensive — no need to widen scope
Single-path implementation is correct without evaluating alternatives first
strength_patterns: Systematic read→edit→test→verify cycles with intermediate checkpoints in complex chains
Consistent and reliable mechanical execution on bounded single-step tasks (style enforcement)
Multi-stage validation before declaring completion — repeated tsc and test-runner passes in long chains
weakness_patterns: Fixation loops on individual files — repeated reads and edits of the same file without stepping back to re-assess the broader state
Shallow alternative exploration — complex implementation chains commit to one approach rather than evaluating competing paths
Silent truncation acceptance — widespread head -N usage without verifying whether critical output was cut off
